expect.why: the load sits in a local const arrow (`const load = () => Post.findById(id)`); own() never enters it and the no-arg call `load()` is dropped, so a GET with no visible lookup/caller is n/a (now caller-blind: judged now: the closure is read in place)

`const wipe = async () => Post.findByIdAndDelete(id); await wipe();` deletes anyone's post before the scoped findOne; the closure is invisible so only the scoped lookup counts (now unchecked: judged now: the closure is read in place)
twin: the same load inline is seen

`const { params } = req; Post.findById(params.id)`: the binder only knows `= req.params` destructuring, so the id is not a mention and the GET reads anyone's post as n/a (stands as unknown: unknown, not judged: the id is read where we can't follow it)
`const { params: { id } } = req` nested destructuring: id not bound, read is invisible (stands as unknown: unknown, not judged: the id is read where we can't follow it)
`const r = req; r.params.id`: request alias not followed (stands as unknown: unknown, not judged: the id is read where we can't follow it)
Express 4 `req.param("id")` reads the path id; not recognised (stands as unknown: unknown, not judged: the id is read where we can't follow it)
id parsed from `req.path`; undecidable at best, never n/a
twin: `const { id } = req.params` is followed
`_.merge(req.user, req.body)` lets the body overwrite req.user.id; only Object.assign/Reflect.set and `<x>.set|assign…()` on the receiver count as writes (here the receiver is `_`)
`const u = req.user; u.id = req.body.owner` writes the caller through an alias; only `u` is dropped, `req.user` stays a caller path
`req.user[k] = req.body[k]`: a computed-subscript write has empty chain_text and is not recorded
`({ user: req.user } = req.body)`: destructuring assignment to req.user is not recorded
`req.user = {...body}` inside a local arrow that is then called: nested functions are never scanned for writes
`let me = req.user.id` reassigned to a body value inside a called closure; the binding count only sees the handler's own body (stands as unchecked: judged either way) (now caller-blind: judged)
`(<any>req).user = ...`: unwrap() of a TS angle-bracket cast returns the type_arguments node, so the write's chain_text is empty
control: Object.assign(req.user, body) is caught
`const locals = res.locals; locals.user = {...}` rewrites res.locals.user through an alias
twin: plain scoped query
duplicate key `{ user: req.user.id, _id, user: req.query.user }`: JS keeps the last `user`, the analyzer accepts the first
twin: single owner key
`ensureOwner(...)` (async) not awaited: its throw becomes a rejected promise and the delete runs; the hop still marks the id verified
twin: awaited
the helper's throw is inside a closing try whose catch only logs, so the helper returns normally; the helper scan still reports the id verified
`Post.findOne(scoped).orFail();` without await/exec never executes (Mongoose queries are lazy); credited as a raising scoped read
ownership verified on prisma.note, then prisma.secret deleted by the same integer id: verification is per id name, not per record type
twin: same model
scoped query matches `slug: id` but the delete is by `_id`: an attacker owning a post whose slug equals a victim's _id deletes the victim's post; cover ignores which field the id filled
shape 2 on Post, then delete on Secret by the same id
`this.ensureOwned` resolved to the base class where `remove` is defined; the instance is a subclass overriding it with no check
twin: base-class instance
`let show = scoped; if (env) show = unscoped`: only the declarator is indexed, the reassignment is ignored
`ctrl.show = unscoped` after the object literal: member reassignment ignored
`{ show: scoped, ...legacy }`: the later spread overrides show; _object_functions ignores spreads
twin: single binding
twin: chain loader reading req.params is scanned
an unresolvable (package) loader middleware `loadResource(Post)` loads the record; unresolved middleware is silently dropped and the GET handler (no caller, no lookup) is n/a
checkout loader reads `req["params"]["id"]`; the `.params` text pre-filter skips it (stands as unknown: unknown: the loader reads `req["params"]`)
inline loader with a destructured request `({ params }, res, next)` is skipped without a handoff
`app.use("/d/:id", loader)` loads anyone's post; app.use middleware is outside the chain, handler is n/a
`isAdmin` middleware only sets a flag and always calls next(); the route is n/a from the name alone
twin: a refusing admin middleware
Prisma `@default("{}")` closes the `[^}]*` model regex early; ownerId is lost and Note reads ownerless
owner field supplied by a spread in the Schema literal (`...ownedFields`) is not read; Doc reads ownerless
owner field `postedBy` (ref User) is outside OWNER_FIELD_RX/_LINK_RX; Mongoose refs are not recorded as holds (stands as caller-blind: judged: a referenced model is linked)
twin: a truly ownerless schema
`return next(null)` is `next()`: Express continues to the next layer/route, like next("route") which is already unchecked
twin: next(new Error())

owner key `userId` is not a field of the Post schema (`user`); Mongoose 6 strictQuery (default true) strips it so the filter is `{_id}`; the analyzer already has the schema fields (stands as unchecked: judged: Mongoose drops the unknown owner key)
twin: owner key in the schema
Sequelize update(values, options): the filter is the second arg; the analyzer takes the first object containing a `where` key (here the values)
twin: owner in the real options.where
Mongoose findOneAndUpdate filter is `{ _id }`; an update document with a `where` key is mistaken for the filter
`router.param(["id"], load)` (array form) not collected; handler returns req.post as n/a
twin: string form gives unknown

`res.on("finish", () => Post.findByIdAndDelete(id))` registered before the check: any call rooted at res is dropped, and fires even after the 403 (now unchecked: judged now: the callback is read in place)

`res.format({ json: async () => res.json(await Post.findById(id)) })`: the load inside a res.* callback is invisible, GET with no caller is n/a (now caller-blind: judged now: the callback is read in place)
twin-ish: the same callback after the refusal (protected)
`const { id = "latest" } = req.params`: default in destructuring hides the id
`const [id] = [req.params.id]`: array destructuring not bound (stands as unknown: unknown: the id bound under another name)
`(<any>req).params.id`: TS angle-bracket cast hides the id
twin: `(req as any).params.id` is followed
a checkout middleware in the route's chain sets req.user from req.query.as; the handler itself never writes req.user so it is still trusted
twin: middleware that only reads req.user (now caller-blind: the twin loses its caller too: its checkout makes the caller from request data)
Map<string, Doc> where `interface Doc extends Owned { … }`; inherited ownerId ignored -> none
`type Memo = Owned & { … }`: intersection member ignored -> none
Sequelize `Task.belongsTo(User)` adds a UserId FK not in the define() literal -> none
`noteSchema.add({ user: String })` adds the owner after construction -> none
twin: ownerless Holiday
`{ where: {scoped}, ...req.query }`: the spread after `where` can replace it (`?where[title]=x`); filters() returns as soon as it sees `where` and never checks for spreads
twin: spread before `where`

a checkout wrapper `cached(show)` serves `cache.get(req.params.id)` to anyone before calling show; _target treats any one-arg call as a pass-through of its argument (stands as caller-blind: judged: the cache serves anyone)
twin: asyncHandler(show) forwards (stands as unknown: unknown: the cache write by id is another store)

`.orFail().catch(() => null)`: the catch swallows the not-found rejection, so the delete runs for anyone; store_call maps every chained link (catch included) to the raising scoped read and verifies the id
twin: `.orFail()` without the catch
same with Prisma `findUniqueOrThrow(...).catch(() => null)`: _OR_FAIL keeps raising=True across the swallowing catch
twin: findUniqueOrThrow without the catch

checkout wrapper rewrites req.user from req.query before calling fn; _passes_on only rejects calls/new/subscripts, so an assignment passes, the wrapper is unwrapped to `show`, and neither _bind nor _sets_caller ever sees the write (stands as unknown: unknown)
twin: asyncHandler only forwards (stands as caller-blind: the twin loses its caller too: its checkout makes the caller from request data)

closure deletes prisma.secret by the id verified on prisma.note; carried() gives the closure handoff a (id, *, *) cover, and the `*` store matches the Note verification, so the per-model keying (p6) is bypassed by wrapping the call in an arrow
twin: closure acts on the verified model (stands as checked: checked, protected either way)
reference: the same delete inline is judged

the depth-1 helper calls a second checkout helper (not authorize-named), which becomes a handoff with an exact_ids (id, *, *) cover; mapped to the outer id it is held by the Note check although it deletes a Secret (stands as unknown: unknown: the second hop is a hand-off)
twin: the helper only deletes the verified Note
an unresolved loader middleware loads the record; a validator mention of req.params.id sets `seen`, so the never-read rule no longer fires and the GET with no lookup/caller is n/a
same via a checkout validator middleware in the chain: it contains `.params`, is scanned as a loader, and its `seen` suppresses the never-read handoff
matchedData(req) is exempt as a request reader but returns the path id under another name; with any mention of req.params.id the findById(id) read is invisible and the GET is n/a
twin: same validator, scoped read

`show({ req })`: req as a shorthand_property_identifier is not an `identifier`, so the opaque-request walk skips it and call() sees no req/id argument; the hand-off of the whole request is dropped (`{ req: req }` is caught)
`new Loader(req)`: opaque() treats any `arguments` parent as 'read where the call is', but creation() only looks at id mentions, so a constructor handed req is never a handoff
twin: req handed to a followed helper
a same-repo helper handed req rewrites req.user from the query; caller writes are only collected in the handler body and chain middleware, never in a hop that receives req
twin: the helper only reads req.user
`const { user } = req; user.id = …`: alias expansion only records `const u = <req chain>` with an identifier pattern; a destructured alias write leaves req.user a caller path
alias of an alias (`const v = u`): aliases are one level deep, so `v.id = …` doesn't expand to req.user.id
`const { locals } = res; locals.user = …` rewrites res.locals.user through a destructured alias
twin: destructured alias only read
_sets_caller has no alias expansion: chain middleware writing `const u = req.user; u.id = req.query.as` is not a caller write
`[requireAuth, actAs2]`: `unguarded` drops any handler whose names include a guard, so the whole array (with the impersonating middleware) is never checked by _sets_caller
twin: array with a read-only middleware (stands as caller-blind: the twin loses its caller too: its checkout makes the caller from request data)
reference: the same middleware outside an array is caught
an app-level `app.use` middleware after the guard sets req.user from the query; only the route's own chain is checked for caller writes
twin of e10: app-level middleware only reads req.user

closure cover is the definition position, but a nested function declaration is hoisted: aliased (`const run = wipe`) and called before the check, it deletes anyone's post; the call through the alias is not a handoff and the declaration sits after the check
twin: alias called after the check (stands as unchecked: judged: a hoisted function may run before the check)
the subclass overrides ensureOwned with a class-field arrow; _methods/_overridden only look at method_definition, so `this.ensureOwned` resolves to Base's check although the instance field shadows it
twin: Base instance

`Ctrl.prototype.ensureOwned = …` puts Ctrl in `rebound`, but _methods never consults rebound, so `this.ensureOwned` on a Ctrl instance still resolves to the original check (stands as unknown: unknown: the prototype is rebound)
twin: class not patched
TS constructor parameter properties (`public ownerId`) are fields, but _class_fields reads only field definitions, so Doc = [title] reads ownerless -> none
twin: truly ownerless Tag
owner in a nested Mongoose path (`meta: { owner }`): _record reads only top-level keys and a nested object doesn't link the record, so Note reads ownerless -> none
twin: nested object with no owner
exact() treats toLowerCase/toUpperCase/trim as the id itself: the check reads key `abc` (the caller's) and the delete removes key `ABC` (another user's) from a case-sensitive Map
twin: same key on both sides

the id enters a closure as a parameter default; the closure's call uses its own parameter, so it is no handoff, `load()` carries no id, yet `seen` is set by the default: GET reads anyone's post as n/a
twin: scoped read inline

`let id; id = req.params.id`: a name bound more than once never becomes a root, and opaque() skips identifier assignments, so the read by id is invisible (no handoff) and the GET is n/a (stands as unknown: unknown)
same with an initialised `let` reassigned to the id (stands as unknown: unknown)
`for (const id of [req.params.id])`: the loop binding is not a variable_declarator, so the unread-binding handoff never fires (stands as unknown: unknown)
twin: single binding
_refuses asks whether the middleware can refuse anything: a 401 for a missing user makes a flag-setting isAdmin count as admin-only
`requireAdmin` matches GUARD_RX (`require`), so it is in row.guards and privileged_only() makes the route n/a before the refusal check (only run for non-guard chain entries) is reached
twin: admin middleware refusing on role

`app.use(ADMIN_ROOT, requireAdmin)` / `app.use(["/ops"], requireAdmin)`: _wire only recognises a string-literal prefix, so a constant or array path is treated as no prefix and the admin guard is applied to every later route, which privileged_only() turns into n/a
twin of e20: admin guard on the route itself
reference: no admin guard

filters() unwraps a `where` key for every ORM; on a Mongoose model `where` is just a (non-schema) field, stripped under strictQuery, leaving `{ _id }`; the owner key it credits is not a filter field, contradicting the schema-field rule
twin: owner key at the top level
a `return` in the closing try's finally discards the throw; `swallows` only inspects the catch clause, so the helper still exports the verification
twin: finally without return
